items.question: Which nutrient mainly gives our body energy?
items.explanation: Carbohydrates are the main energy-giving food. Rice, wheat, potatoes and sugar are rich in them. Fats also give energy, while vitamins and minerals keep the body working well.

items.question: Proteins help our body grow and repair itself.
items.explanation: Proteins are called body-building foods. They help build muscles and repair injuries. Pulses (dal), milk, eggs and paneer are good sources of protein.

items.question: A long-term lack of vitamin C in food can cause which disease?
items.explanation: Scurvy causes bleeding gums and slow healing of wounds. Vitamin C is found in fruits like amla, oranges and lemons. Long ago, sailors on long trips often got scurvy because they had no fresh fruit.

items.fact: Roughage (dietary fibre) gives no energy, but it helps food move smoothly through the intestines.
items.explanation: Roughage is found in whole grains, fruits, vegetables and pulses. Our body cannot digest it, but it helps get rid of undigested food.

items.question: Which vitamin can our skin make when it is exposed to sunlight?
items.explanation: When sunlight falls on our skin, the body makes vitamin D. Vitamin D helps us use calcium to build strong bones and teeth. That is why it is sometimes called the "sunshine vitamin".
